reason: Implausible content: an auto-rickshaw ride 'to Mumbai' for a hundred rupees does not make sense, so the sentence reads as translationese. Minimal fix – same structure and vocabulary, realistic destination, which is exactly the haggling phrase a learner needs.

reason: Unnatural and poetic: the original has no subject at all ('कागज़ की कश्ती … तैराई') and echoes a well-known ghazal lyric; कश्ती is literary. Replacement supplies the agent and uses the ordinary word नाव, keeping the same node-21 perfective with feminine object agreement.

reason: Implausible scope – nobody is voted 'the best employee in Chennai'; the city-wide framing makes the sentence read as machine-generated. Minimal fix keeps the identical node-22 passive (को … चुना गया) with a realistic scope.

oldTarget: तनवी न सिर्फ़ परीक्षा में पास हुई, बल्कि अव्वल भी आई।

reason: Gender mismatch: रूबी is a woman's name but the verb is masculine होगा, so the model sentence is grammatically wrong. Swapped in a male name to keep the same ज़रूर + future pattern.
